## V. CONCLUSIONS

In this  paper; we propose BLS-EDMD method for approximating the Koopman   operator  and use this   method to design a new MPC. This method solves the problem of model prediction error caused by the randomness associated with the choice of basis functions in the traditional EDMD method. By leveraging the feature and enhancement layers of the BLS network, the   generation  of basis functions, thereby enhancing the state represen tation and boosting the model's overall prediction accuracy. In simulation experiments; we apply the proposed method to the target tracking control task of a classical van der Pol oscillator system and results show that the BLS-EDMD-based Koopman predictor has significant advantages in terms of accuracy and stability. In   addition; the control accuracy of the BLS-EDMD-based MPC controller is effectively  validated in complex DSRV scenario; highlighting its potential to effectively handle high dimensional nonlinear systems. system

In future work we will further extend the current BE MPC methodology for applications in more complex nonlinear dynamic systems, such as multi-degree-of-freedom UUV and underwater devices with more complex hydrodynamic proper ties.
